change_summary: The journal retracted "Caffeine improves working memory in adults". An institutional investigation found that the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated, and the notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The paper's Results section uses those figures for its n-back accuracy finding, so its main result is affected. The authors have not responded.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and gives that as the reason you chose a 200 mg dose. The stored paper reports that 12% improvement in its Section 3.2, and the retraction says the data in Figures 2 to 4 were fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. So the rationale for your dose choice rests on a retracted result. This matters a lot for that sentence; it is the only citation of the paper in your draft.
recommendation: Remove or replace the Introduction citation of Brown and Kim [3], because the journal has retracted the article and the notice says its data in Figures 2 to 4 were fabricated. The 12% improvement at 200 mg that your draft uses to justify its dose is the paper's reported result, so find another basis for the dose choice.
